historyTimeline.h2: Land Rover Defender 110 2.4 TDCi - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: When the 2.4 TDCi "Puma" launched in the Defender 110, it replaced the older Td5, introducing a modern Ford-sourced Duratorq diesel architecture with improved emissions compliance and the distinctive bonnet bulge.

milestones.description: 244DT (2.4L, 122hp) introduced to the Defender 110, featuring a variable geometry turbocharger and common-rail injection.
Minor updates to the EGR and turbo wastegate solenoid systems to address early reliability feedback and improve boost control.
2.4 TDCi phased out in the Defender 110, replaced by the 2.2 TDCi (DT224) to meet stricter Euro 5 emissions standards.

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Land Rover Defender 110 2.4 TDCi is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Land Rover Defender 110 2.4 TDCi Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The 244DT engine dominating the Land Rover Defender 110 2.4 TDCi is generally robust but suffers from specific Ford Duratorq-era weaknesses, particularly around the turbocharger and emissions systems. Rebuilt 244DT engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing these original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Turbo Wastegate & EGR Fouling - Why the Land Rover Defender 110 2.4 TDCi 244DT Loses Power
problems.rootCause: Carbon buildup in the EGR valve restricts airflow, while the turbo wastegate solenoid vacuum lines degrade, causing boost control failure and triggering limp mode.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Cleaning the EGR valve, replacing the wastegate solenoid, and checking vacuum lines.
repairOptions.longevity: Good short-term fix if turbo internals are healthy and no metallic debris is present.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of a fully rebuilt 244DT with a pre-checked turbo, revised EGR setup, and 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: The right call if the turbo has failed catastrophically, sending debris into the engine, or if there is significant bottom-end wear.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: Classic Land Rover Defender 110 Puma (2007-2011) values remain strong, typically ranging from £8,000 to £18,000+ depending on spec, mileage, and condition [THIRD-PARTY]. Because the vehicle worth is well above £8,000, a £3,200-£4,800 rebuilt engine replacement cost is typically a sound investment that preserves the vehicle's usability and classic market value ( Safe).
problems.recommendation: If your Land Rover Defender 110 2.4 TDCi is only showing early signs of limp mode with no metallic knocking or excessive oil consumption, a specialist EGR clean, EGR blanking (where legally permissible for off-road use), and wastegate solenoid replacement is the most cost-effective route. However, if the turbo has failed and contaminated the engine with swarf, a full rebuilt unit is the only reliable long-term solution.

items.question: What are the signs of turbo failure in a Land Rover Defender 110 2.4 TDCi?
items.answer: The 244DT engine is prone to turbo wastegate solenoid failure and EGR fouling, which can escalate to full turbo failure if ignored. Watch for early warning signs.
keyPoints: Sudden loss of power or the vehicle entering "limp mode" on hills.
Excessive blue or grey smoke from the exhaust under acceleration.
A high-pitched whining or whistling noise from the engine bay.

items.question: How long does a Land Rover Defender 110 2.4 TDCi engine replacement take?
items.answer: Because the 244DT is a longitudinally mounted engine with ample bay space, a specialist workshop can typically complete the swap efficiently.
keyPoints: Engine removal and refitting usually takes 10 to 14 hours of labour.
Total workshop turnaround is typically 3 to 5 working days.
Additional time may be required if the clutch or flywheel needs replacing simultaneously.

items.question: What is the difference between the Land Rover Defender 110 2.4 TDCi and 2.2 TDCi engines?
items.answer: While both are Ford-sourced Duratorq diesels, the 2.2 TDCi (DT224) was introduced in 2012 to meet stricter Euro 5 emissions standards, bringing notable changes.
keyPoints: The 2.2 TDCi features a different turbocharger setup and revised EGR system.
The 2.4 TDCi is generally considered to have a slightly more robust bottom end by enthusiasts.
The 2.2 TDCi is more complex electronically, making the 2.4 TDCi a favourite for simpler mechanical repairs.
